import concurrent.futures,json,time
def run(q):

        q.case('drain','explicit_fixture_requalification_'+flag,q.sql('SELECT 1;','test_verifier',ok=False).returncode==0,'fixture controller explicitly clears flag; no automatic ownership release')
    q.ex('touch','/run/flooow-watchdog/cancel-failure','/run/flooow-watchdog/terminate-failure')
    with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1) as pool:
        writer=pool.submit(q.sql,'SELECT pg_sleep(20);','test_verifier',False);time.sleep(1);q.paused.set()
        with q.health_lock:
            x=dict(q.expected_status);x['state']='REVOKED';q.rootfile('/run/flooow-external/status.json',json.dumps(x));q.observer_once()
        q.denial('drain','signals_unavailable_no_new_admission')
        with q.health_lock:
            q.rootfile('/run/flooow-external/status.json',json.dumps(q.expected_status));assert q.observer_once()
        # Even fresh eligibility cannot bypass the unresolved existing quarantine.
        q.denial('drain','current_custody_cannot_bypass_live_quarantine')
        q.ex('rm','-f','/run/flooow-watchdog/terminate-failure');result=writer.result(timeout=10);time.sleep(.2)
        absent=q.sql("SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE usename='test_verifier';").stdout.strip()=='0'
        q.case('drain','kernel_and_catalog_stop_required',result.returncode!=0 and absent,{'backend_exit':result.returncode,'catalog_disappeared':absent,'effects':'UNKNOWN_REQUIRES_RECONCILIATION','ownership_release':False})
        q.ex('rm','-f','/run/flooow-watchdog/cancel-failure');q.paused.clear()
    # Regression must pass on the final receiver variant too.
    q.ex('touch','/run/flooow-watchdog/crash-supervisor')
    end=time.monotonic()+10
    while time.monotonic()<end and q.ex('pg_isready','-h','/tmp/pgsock','-U','postgres',ok=False).returncode==0:time.sleep(.1)
    gone=q.ex('pg_isready','-h','/tmp/pgsock','-U','postgres',ok=False).returncode!=0
    if not gone:raise RuntimeError('Final receiver failed supervisor-loss regression')
    q.boot()
    with q.health_lock:assert q.observer_once()
    q.case('restart','final_receiver_supervisor_restart',q.sql('SELECT 1;','test_verifier',ok=False).returncode==0,'expected parent peer pidfd matches retained supervisor anchor; fresh epoch')

# Full synthetic binding/enforcement qualification successor

Explicitly authorized TEST_ONLY_NONCANONICAL experiment, independently isolated
from canonical V6. It is not a production component or a full V043 deployment.
The evidence directory records both implementation and remaining HOLDs.

The builder derives native successor files from frozen predecessor sources. It
never edits those predecessors or executes migrations. It copies exact V043
header/lifecycle/attempt-pointer DDL into synthetic fixtures, uses the normative
38-tag binding framing, and retains the two additional physical header columns.
The external observer verifies an independently pinned synthetic original bundle
with Ed25519/OpenSSL, current root-owned custody/status/target association and the
full protected header. The receiver independently verifies role/slot/catalog and
retained kernel anchors. This synthetic consumer is not the complete frozen
V043/S02/JVM domain validation path; parity remains explicitly unqualified.

Requirements: Python, Docker, the pinned preexisting PostgreSQL18.4 image, and
the explicit disposable implementation plus test-only signing grants. The scoped
seccomp profile is inherited unchanged from predecessor evidence. The existing
ICU76 runtime implements strict UTF8/NFC without installing a library. The exact
official libpq header is fetched with a pinned SHA256; no package is installed.

```powershell
python scripts/validation/package_0090_full_qualification/build.py --output C:\Users\xmz_r\AppData\Local\Temp\flooow-full-new-evidence
```

An existing output directory or container name is refused. Optional separate
scenario modules are `supplement`, `restart_probe` and `drain_probe`. Every run
gets fresh synthetic IDs and an Ed25519 key generated solely in a root-only
container tmpfs directory. Private key bytes never reach the host or evidence.
The observer has Docker control of the owned container; service SQL does not.
This is a trusted harness/control plane, not hostile administrator protection.

Finally cleanup erases the test private key and removes the exactly owned,
labelled, image-pinned container. Network is none, no host mounts/ports, CPU quota
one and memory768MiB. Load is bounded CPU work and 8MiB tmpfs write loops. Abrupt
host process death may prevent finally; inspect exact ownership before manual
cleanup. Unrelated resources are never cleanup targets.

The 5s abort/health lease, 200ms cancellation escalation, polling, capacity,
resource and subprocess limits are separately recorded experimental controls.
None confers numeric policy authority. The policy digest here represents test
structure association; no complete approved numeric29-field policy is provisioned.
No canonical readiness, key, approval, ID, ADMIN, T0, SIGN, TREG or final runner
is consumed. Synthetic signing is performed under its explicit narrow grant.

Coverage gaps remain for complete pre-enrollment backend observability, full
frozen verifier/domain/ownership parity, allocator OID reuse/tombstones and
worst-case observation/scheduling bounds. HOLD is a valid documented outcome.
